title: RDS Performance Insights Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.1.62 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.1.62 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=aws` sourcetype=`aws:cloudwatch` collected via `Splunk_TA_aws`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/RDS" metric_name="DBLoad" statistic="Average"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.62_rds_performance_insights_62"
| sort -_time
description: Performance Insights exposes DB load by wait state; trending top SQL and waits guides index and instance right-sizing beyond raw CPU.
value: Detecting rds performance insights trending early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Enable Performance Insights (7–30 day retention). Export `DBLoad`, `DBLoadCPU`, `DBLoadNonCPU` via API or CloudWatch where available. Alert on sustained elevation vs weekly baseline. Join with application release times.
visualization: Line chart (DB load vs baseline), Table (instance, wait class if ingested), Area chart (CPU vs non-CPU load).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` max(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as load_proxy
  from datamodel=Performance.All_Performance
  where match(Performance.object, "(?i)dbinstance|RDS|aws/rds")
  by Performance.object span=1h
| sort - load_proxy
dataModelAcceleration: Performance: `DBLoad` in raw CloudWatch/PI is the primary; CIM tstats is a stand-in for mapped DB host metrics. Enable Data Model Acceleration for the CIM data models in `cimModels` once `Splunk_TA_aws` (and any CIM tags/aliases) map your fields; otherwise the `cimSpl` summary search may be empty. Step 2 on raw or metric indexes stays primary for most sites.
knownFalsePositives: Large ad hoc queries, ETL, or an index build that you expect to spike DB load during the same maintenance window as the alert.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=aws`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_aws` with the modular input for `aws:cloudwatch`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.1.78.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `metric_name` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Enable Performance Insights (7–30 day retention). Export `DBLoad`, `DBLoadCPU`, `DBLoadNonCPU` via API or CloudWatch where available. Alert on sustained elevation vs weekly baseline. Join with application release times.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=aws sourcetype="aws:cloudwatch" namespace="AWS/RDS" metric_name="DBLoad" statistic="Average"
| table _time metric_name namespace unit average maximum
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.1.62_rds_performance_insights_62"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `aws:cloudwatch` in `index=aws` to detect rds performance insights trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the Amazon CloudWatch console Metrics for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `metric_name` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_1_62_alert` with severity aligned to `medium` criticality. Dashboard: Line chart (DB load vs baseline), Table (instance, wait class if ingested), Area chart (CPU vs non-CPU load)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_aws` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of rds performance insights trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
